text: CHAPTER 15
speaker: Narrator

text: The Ledger's Margin
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The walk back from the east gate took longer than the morning's survey. The rain that had threatened the lower districts since noon finally broke, not in a clean downpour, but in a thin, greasy mist that turned the dust in the unpaved alleys into gray paste.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag pulled his wool cloak tighter over his shoulders, his boots making a wet, sucking sound in the lane.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: If it keeps up like this, the foundations on the south quarter are going to float before we finish the month.
speaker: Balag

text: They aren't going to float,
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu said, stepping carefully around a broken drainage tile.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: They're going to settle. Which means the temple will have to pay twice as much for shoring next season. The water's just doing the math for them.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Ninsun walked between them, her head down, holding her satchel tight against her chest to keep the damp off the paper. Her boots were caked in the same commercial mortar dust Zik had noticed earlier, the gray residue that didn't match the temple mix.
speaker: Narrator

text: They reached the room without running into the Collector or anyone else who looked like they had business with them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag dropped the survey rods by the door, unlatched the shutter to let the stale air out, and dropped onto his bench without lighting the lamp. The room went gray as the daylight faded through the unglazed window frame.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun didn't sit. She laid her map out on the pine table, smoothing the curled edges of the parchment with the flat of her hand. The four boxes—CLAIMED, COST, LIMIT, and the empty space she'd left after the east wall—were barely visible in the dim light.
speaker: Narrator

text: She picked up her stylus, hovered the metal point over the blank space beside the east-side survey mark, and then stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik set his pack down by the threshold. He didn't take anything out.
speaker: Narrator

text: You're not marking it,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Ninsun kept the stylus steady, though her hand cast a long, shaky shadow across the parchment under the gray light from the window.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't have a name for this box yet.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Call it what it is,
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu said, leaning against the doorframe while she wrung the mist from the fringe of her shawl.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Inventory.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Balag let out a short, rough breath that sounded almost like a laugh.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The city's keeping score. We're just writing down the numbers.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik walked over to the table and looked down at the map. The defaced spiral-drop Ninsun had drawn in the corner sat right on the boundary line between the east wall and the lower tanneries, as if the same crack ran underneath both of them without caring about the distance.
speaker: Narrator

text: He reached out, took the small ceramic ink-pot by its neck, and moved it two inches to the left, covering the empty space entirely.
speaker: Narrator

text: Leave it blank,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Ninsun looked up at him, her eyes dark in the failing light. For a second she looked like she wanted to argue, to reach for the stylus and scratch the word down anyway before the dark took the room. Then she slowly lowered her hand, the metal point resting against the grain of the wood beside the paper.
speaker: Narrator

text: We can't leave it blank,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said, her voice dropping into a sharper, harder register.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Not after what we saw on the curtain wall. The temple survey codes don't match the commercial stock. That means the records were altered twice—once when the wall went up, and again when they tried to scrape the name out.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu pushed off the doorframe, her interest suddenly sharp.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You're saying the east-side survey isn't the whole record.
speaker: Enhedu

text: I'm saying the public registry only shows what the temple wanted kept after the second consolidation,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said, tapping the edge of her uninked stylus against the table.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: If we want to know whose name was under that defaced seal, we aren't going to find it on the outside of the wall.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Where, then?
speaker: Balag

text: Balag asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The lower archive branch behind the third district weigh-station,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The old tax ledgers from before the plague years. The ones the Collector said stay locked.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik looked at the ink-pot covering the empty box on the map. He didn't reach for his pack. He didn't look for an excuse to wait.
speaker: Narrator

text: Grab the lantern,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: If we get to the weigh-station before the evening shift changes, the night clerk won't check the seals on the side bins.
speaker: Zik

text: Balag stood up, his boots hitting the floorboards with a dull, heavy jar, and reached for his spear. Enhedu was already sliding her ledger into her pack.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun picked up her stylus, tucked it behind her ear, and rolled the map tight.
speaker: Narrator

text: They left the room without looking back.
speaker: Narrator

text: The rain had thickened by the time they reached the third district weigh-station.
speaker: Narrator
